question: The anterior pituitary gland:

options.opa: It is part of the hypothalamus.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "part of the endocrine system" -> "regulated by hypothalamic hormones" -> "hormonal regulation" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "produces and releases hormones" -> "regulated by releasing and inhibiting hormones from the hypothalamus" -> "hormonally regulated" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "communicates with the neurohypophysis" -> "via the hypothalamic-pituitary axis" -> "indirect communication" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "does not release ADH and oxytocin" -> "these are released by the posterior pituitary" -> "incorrect statement" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Anterior pituitary gland" -> "formed by glandular epithelial tissue" -> "not formed by neurons" -> "incorrect statement" -> 75%
analysis: The anterior pituitary gland is not part of the hypothalamus; it is regulated hormonally by releasing and inhibiting hormones from the hypothalamus. It does not communicate with the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) in the same way, and it does not release ADH and oxytocin, which are released by the posterior pituitary. The anterior pituitary is formed from epithelial tissue, not neurons.
